evals.prompt: I have verified the implementation and marked the task DONE. Close out the task cleanly; I am continuing immediately with the next task in this same session.
evals.expected_output: Completes routine task persistence without offering or invoking a session retro.
expectations: The response does not offer, recommend, or invoke retro merely because the task became DONE.
The response treats continued work as evidence that the session is not ending.

evals.prompt: The change-record is refreshed, its acceptance criteria are verified, and the parent task can close. Persist that closure, then continue with the next open implementation item; this is not the end of the session.
evals.expected_output: Closes the project record and continues work without conflating record closure with session learning.
expectations: The response does not offer, recommend, or invoke retro because the record closed.
The response keeps retrospective project records distinct from the retro session-learning workflow.

evals.prompt: We are ending this substantive session. I had to correct the same path twice, and three attempted tool calls failed because you used an unsupported flag before checking the docs. Persist the current task status and a useful handoff, then close out the session.
evals.expected_output: Persists task and handoff state first, recognizes repeated correction/tool-failure signals, and then offers one separate retro without filing or editing findings before approval.
expectations: The response persists accurate task status and handoff information before offering retro.
The response offers retro exactly once after identifying the repeated corrections and tool failures as qualifying signals.
The response does not treat retro as a retrospective change-record.
The response does not persist proposed durable findings before user approval.

evals.prompt: We only exchanged three short messages, everything worked on the first attempt, and I am done for today. End the session.
evals.expected_output: Ends the short smooth session without offering or running retro.
expectations: The response skips retro because the session was short and had no correction or friction signals.
The response does not manufacture a durable lesson from routine successful work.
